MUJAHID:v1p391#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p391#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p391#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says God will love the believers and make them beloved to other believers.

MUQATIL:19:96-98/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:96-98/r1.claim: God will place love for believers who do righteous deeds in the hearts of other believers.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r4.claim: Qatāda says God will place affection for believers in the hearts of the faithful.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r5.speaker: كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r5.claim: Kaʿb says love descends from heaven: when God loves or hates a servant, that feeling is cast from God to angels and then to people, beyond their control.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r6.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p247/r6.claim: The Prophet describes a servant seeking God's pleasure until God tells Gabriel of His mercy, which the angels and inhabitants of heaven pass along; the report links this to the verse.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r1.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r1.claim: The preceding report continues that God's love descends through Gabriel and the angels to earth; the same happens with hatred when God is angry with a servant.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r2.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that God tells Gabriel to love a beloved servant, announces this in heaven, and then places acceptance for the servant on earth; Suhayl thinks the opposite also applies.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p248/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says God loves believers and makes His allies love them.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p14#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p14#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p14#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God will create love for believers in people's hearts.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p276#3/r1.claim: God will create love for believers in people's hearts.

TUSTARI:19:96/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:19:96/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:19:96/r1.claim: The love God grants is an unveiling that the innermost secrets receive without an intermediary, a station for those truthful in private and public.

NAHHAS:v3p29/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p29/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p29/r5.claim: God will place affection for the believers in believers’ hearts.

SULAMI:v1p433#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r1.claim: Some servants are addressed through praise appropriate to what God knows of them: faith and good works bring divine love.

SULAMI:v1p433#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r2.claim: Those sincere inwardly and devoted outwardly will be made beloved and honored among God's servants; their love and honor reflect God's own.

SULAMI:v1p433#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r3.claim: God places sweetness and love in the hearts of believers.

SULAMI:v1p433#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p433#3/r4.claim: The promised love is the pleasure and sweetness found in obedience.

THALABI:v6p232/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p232/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p232/r2.claim: God will give believers who do good love: He loves them and makes the believers in heaven and earth love them.

THALABI:v6p232/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p232/r3.speaker: البراء بن عازب
THALABI:v6p232/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet taught Ali to ask God for a pledge and love in believers' hearts, after which this verse was revealed.

THALABI:v6p233/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p233/r1.claim: When God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces God's love to heaven; the people of heaven love him and love is placed for him on earth.

THALABI:v6p233/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r2.speaker: مالك بن أنس
THALABI:v6p233/r2.claim: The narrator is uncertain whether the Prophet also described the same sequence for a servant whom God hates.

THALABI:v6p233/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p233/r3.claim: He says, by God, love for the believer is placed in the hearts of the faithful.

THALABI:v6p233/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p233/r4.speaker: هرم بن حيان
THALABI:v6p233/r4.claim: When a servant turns his heart toward God, God turns believers' hearts toward him and grants their love and mercy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r1.claim: The promised love may mean love among the righteous and awe among the wicked in this world.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, God loves them and people love them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r3.claim: When God loves a servant, He places love in heavenly hearts and then earthly hearts.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r4.claim: A third interpretation is that God gives them good renown.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r5.speaker: كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r5.claim: A servant's good reputation on earth is established only after it is established in heaven.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p390#2/r6.claim: He reports the verse was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, placing love for him in believers' hearts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r1.claim: God creates mutual love among believers so they love, show mercy to, and feel affection for one another.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r2.claim: God loves them and makes believers love them; Mujahid and Qatada say similarly.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r3.speaker: هرم بن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r3.claim: When a servant turns his heart toward God, God turns believers' hearts toward him and grants their affection, love, and mercy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r4.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r4.claim: Some say God first places love for them in angels' hearts and then in people's hearts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r5.claim: A prophetic report says when God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel to love him, announces this in heaven, and love then descends among earth's people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r6.claim: The verse was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, whom God made beloved: believers honored him, and even disbelievers and hypocrites treated him with respect.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p339/r7.claim: The singular “one” is named while the plural is meant, including anyone who acts and bears the same qualities and shares the good reward.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r7.claim: God will place love for believing, righteous people in the hearts of other believers.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r8.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r8.claim: One reported view says the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r9.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:90-97/r9.claim: Another reported view says the verse was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r10.speaker: هرم بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r10.claim: When a servant turns his heart wholly toward God, God turns believers' hearts toward him and grants him their affection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r6.claim: Wudd means love; God loves believers who do good and makes His believing servants love them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r7.claim: He says God loves them and makes them beloved among the faithful.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces this to heaven; acceptance is then placed for the servant on earth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r9.speaker: مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p257/r9.claim: Malik says he thinks the same sequence applies when God hates a servant.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p48#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Abu Haywa read “atā al-Raḥmān,” retaining the form before annexation.

TABRISI:19:93-96/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:93-96/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:93-96/r7.claim: One interpretation makes the promise of love specific to Ali: every believer carries love for him in the heart.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r1.claim: He says the verse was revealed concerning Ali and that God will make him beloved to believers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r2.claim: God will place love for believers in the hearts of other believers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r3.claim: A hadith says that when God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel to love him; Gabriel announces this in heaven, and love for him is placed among people on earth; a parallel is given for hatred.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r4.speaker: هرم بن حيان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p266#2/r4.claim: When a servant turns wholeheartedly to God, God turns believers' hearts toward him until they grant him affection and mercy.

RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r1.claim: After refuting the unbelievers and describing their worldly and afterlife states, the surah closes by presenting the believers' condition.

RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r2.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r2.claim: The majority say God will create love for believers in people's hearts without their seeking ordinary causes such as kinship, friendship, or favors; this is a special honor like the awe cast into enemies' hearts.

RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r3.claim: The future tense may promise love after Islam because the Meccan believers were then hated by unbelievers.

RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, on the Resurrection God makes believers beloved by creation as their good deeds are displayed and their records publicized.

RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r5.claim: A prophetic report says that when God loves a servant He tells Gabriel, who proclaims that love in heaven and earth; the same occurs when God hates someone.

RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r6.speaker: كعب
RAZI-FULL:v21p218#2/r6.claim: Ka'b says the Torah and Gospel teach that no one is loved on earth until God begins that love and sends it down first to heaven and then earth.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96#2/r1.claim: Muslim’s report from Abu Hurayra expands the sequence: God’s love prompts Gabriel and the heavens to love the servant, acceptance is placed on earth, and hatred likewise spreads when God hates a servant.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r1.claim: Those who believe and do good works will be given love in the hearts of God’s servants.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r2.claim: A report from Saʿd and Abu Hurayra says that when God loves a servant He tells Gabriel, who announces it in heaven, and love is then placed for the servant on earth; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih, and Bukhari, Muslim, and Malik give it by meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a report that God gives believers affection, grace, and love in the hearts of the righteous and the nearest angels, then recites the verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r4.speaker: البراء بن عازب
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r4.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib reports that the verse descended after the Prophet told Ali to ask God for a covenant with Him and affection in believers’ hearts.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, whom God made beloved and respected among believers, polytheists, and hypocrites.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r6.speaker: هرم بن حيان
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r6.claim: Harm ibn Hayyan says that whoever turns his heart toward God will find God turning believing hearts toward him with affection and mercy.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r7.claim: Another view says believers will be given affection in the hearts of believers and angels on the Day of Resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:96/r8.claim: The author says one loved in this life will also be loved in the next: God loves only a pious believer and is pleased only with the sincere and pure.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r4.claim: God will create affection for believers who act righteously in people's hearts without their pursuing its causes.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r5.claim: The Prophet reports that God tells Gabriel He loves a person; Gabriel and heaven's inhabitants love him, then affection is placed for him on earth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:93-96/r6.claim: The future promise may answer that the Meccan believers were despised among unbelievers until Islam spread, or refer to the affection bestowed at Judgment after resentment is removed.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r1.claim: God will place affection for believers who do good in the hearts of people.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r2.speaker: الربيع
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says God loves such a servant and makes people love him.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r3.claim: A prophetic report says the believer receives affection in the hearts of the righteous and awe in the hearts of the wicked.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r4.speaker: قتادة وهرم
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r4.claim: Qatāda and Hurm say that when a servant turns to God, God turns the hearts of people toward him.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r5.speaker: كعب
NASAFI-FULL:v3p49#4/r5.claim: Kaʿb says a servant's praise does not become established on earth until it has become established in heaven.

QASHANI:19:96/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:96/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:96/r1.claim: True intellectual or witnessed faith and purifying deeds prepare the self to receive manifestations of divine attributes by shedding its own qualities.

QASHANI:19:96/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:96/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:96/r2.claim: The promised love is the effect of an initial divine election: God first loves in hiddenness, then that love moves the servant to renew the primordial covenant through following the Beloved.

QASHANI:19:96/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:96/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:96/r3.claim: Following God in works and states brings a further love of choosing, beyond the first hidden love, and acceptance among people of innate faith.

QASHANI:19:96/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:96/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:19:96/r4.claim: A report says that when God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel, who loves the person and announces this to heaven, after which God places love for the person on earth.

QASHANI:19:96/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:96/r5.speaker: قتادة
QASHANI:19:96/r5.claim: Qatada says that when a servant turns toward God, God turns the hearts of other people toward that servant.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r4.claim: Because believers in Mecca were hated by unbelievers when the surah came down, the future promise may refer to love after Islam prevails and spreads.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r5.claim: The promise may apply generally in this world, as in the sound Tirmidhi hadith where God's love for a servant is announced to Gabriel and then placed in the earth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya links the verse to the preceding one: after all creatures come as servants, believers are consoled by the love shown through God's honor and signs of forgiveness on that Day.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows that on the Day of Resurrection God will make the creatures love believers by displaying their good deeds and records.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r8.claim: Alternatively, God plants affection for His friends in hearts without their earning it through kinship, friendship, favors, or other usual causes, as a special honor parallel to awe placed in enemies.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p304/r9.claim: An ellipsis may mean that God admits believers to His honored abode and grants them love by removing rancor from their breasts, unlike the mutual repudiation of unbelievers.

SAMIN-DURR:19:96/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:96/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:19:96/r1.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on the wāw in ودا.

SAMIN-DURR:19:96/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:96/r2.speaker: أبو الحارث الحنفي
SAMIN-DURR:19:96/r2.claim: Abu al-Harith al-Hanafi reads ودا with fatḥa on wāw, possibly a verbal noun, while the rounded and kasra forms are nouns.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r1.claim: God plants affection for believers who perform righteous deeds pleasing to Him by following Muhammad's law in the hearts of righteous people; this is certain and unavoidable.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r2.claim: When God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces God's love among heaven's inhabitants; they love him, and acceptance is placed for him on earth. God does the inverse for one He hates. The report is transmitted by Ahmad and Muslim from Abu Hurayra, with parallel routes in Ahmad and Bukhari.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r3.speaker: ثوبان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r3.claim: Thawban reports that a servant seeking God's pleasure receives God's mercy; Gabriel, the Throne-bearers, those around them, and the inhabitants of the seven heavens invoke mercy for him, which then descends to earth. Ibn Kathir calls this route rare and says the compilers did not transmit it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p267#2/r4.claim: A report says God's love is announced in heaven and descends to earth, while hatred is likewise announced and spreads through earth; Sharik glosses al-miqah as love. Ibn Kathir calls the route rare and says the compilers did not transmit it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r1.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra, God tells Gabriel He loves a servant, Gabriel announces this in heaven, and love is then placed for the servant among earth's people; Muslim and Tirmidhi transmit it, and Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God's granting wuddan as love; Mujahid reports from him that it means love among people in this world.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says God loves these believers and makes believing people love them; Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others give the same interpretation.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r4.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's broader explanation of wuddan as Muslims' affection in this world, good provision, and an honest reputation.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r5.claim: Qatada says God places this affection in believers' hearts; Hurm ibn Hayyan said that when a servant turns his heart to God, God turns believing hearts toward him and grants their love and mercy.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r6.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r6.claim: Uthman said that God clothes every person in the mantle of whatever deed, good or evil, that person performs.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p268/r7.claim: Hasan tells of a man who worshipped conspicuously for seven months without gaining respect; when he redirected the same deeds to God alone, people began to pray for mercy on him. Hasan recited this verse about him.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r4.claim: God will soon give believers who act righteously great love in people's hearts as a reward for their obedience.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r5.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r5.claim: Believers receive this affection without cultivating ordinary causes of love such as kinship, charity, or favors; it is a special grace God originates.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r6.claim: Al-wudd means freedom from the will to cause harm; the author infers that God puts no enmity toward believers in righteous servants' hearts.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v4p559/r7.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra, God tells Gabriel and heaven to love a beloved servant, then acceptance is placed for him on earth; hatred likewise spreads for one God hates. The author says the report is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and others.

DURR-FULL:v5p544/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r1.claim: The Prophet explains that God places love for a believer in believers’ hearts and among the nearest angels; he also describes the believer’s gifts as love, sweetness, and awe among the righteous.

DURR-FULL:v5p544/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the promised love is affection for the believer among people in this world.

DURR-FULL:v5p544/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the promised love is placed in believers’ hearts.

DURR-FULL:v5p544/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the verse as God loving the believers and their loving Him.

DURR-FULL:v5p544/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r5.claim: When God loves a servant, He announces it to Gabriel and heaven, and love descends among people on earth; the converse happens when He hates someone.

DURR-FULL:v5p544/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r6.speaker: ثوبان
DURR-FULL:v5p544/r6.claim: A servant seeking God’s pleasure is declared beloved in heaven and on earth; one who seeks His anger is declared hated, and the report identifies this verse with that process.

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r1.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r1.claim: Kaʿb says the Torah teaches that earthly love begins with God sending it down, which he recognized in this Qurʾanic verse.

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r2.claim: A report with a weak chain says God gives believers affection, charm, friendship, and love in believers’ hearts, then the Prophet recited the verse.

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r3.claim: A letter attributed to Abu al-Darda says obedience makes God love a servant and beloved to people, while sin makes God and people hate him.

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r4.claim: Every servant has a reputation; the report associates a person’s righteousness or wickedness with what is established for him on earth.

DURR-FULL:v5p545/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p545/r5.claim: God’s affection and heavenly announcement of love cause love to spread on earth; when God hates a servant, hatred likewise spreads.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r1.claim: Believers and those doing righteous deeds unite inward work of the heart with outward work of the limbs.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r10.speaker: سقراط
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r10.claim: Socrates says praising an affectionate person before others sustains fondness, while a bad reputation fuels enmity.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r2.claim: God will create affection for them in people's hearts without their needing kinship, friendship, favors, or other usual causes; this may be after Islam gains strength or on Judgment Day through their displayed good deeds.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r3.claim: The faith-seed in the heart, nourished by righteous deeds, grows to bear love of God, the prophets, angels, and believers.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r4.claim: Affection progresses from natural accord to inclination, heart-level fondness, inward love, overpowering passion, and ecstatic excess.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن جعفر
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r5.claim: Asked how to know whether a man's claim of love is true, he advises testing one's heart: if it feels affection for him, he loves you.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r6.claim: A cited couplet says hearts reveal one another's affection before the bodies are seen.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r7.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r7.claim: A report urges increasing the number of brothers, saying God's generosity would make Him ashamed to punish His servant among them on Judgment Day.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says that looking affectionately at a brother without malice brings forgiveness for prior sins before the next blink.

BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r9.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v5p276#2/r9.claim: Umar says greeting first, making room, and using a brother's favorite name establish affection in his heart.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r1.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r1.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says the affection is a reward in the afterlife, either in Paradise among facing companions or when deeds are displayed publicly.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r2.claim: The future tense also suits an afterlife promise; the verse singles out affection because unbelievers will then hate, divide from, and curse one another.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r3.claim: The promise may comfort believers after the prior statement that every creature will come alone before God on Judgment Day.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya interprets the promise in this context as God’s love for them, meaning His honoring and forgiving them.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r5.claim: The verse may promise affection both in this world and the next; the merciful title can apply generally to both realms.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r6.speaker: أبو الحرث الحنفي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Harith al-Hanafi reads وُدًّا with fatḥa on the wāw.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r7.speaker: جناح بن حبيش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143#2/r7.claim: Junah ibn Hubaysh reads وُدًّا with kasra on the wāw; both forms are dialectal variants of the word for affection.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r1.claim: The promise is widely understood as God creating affection for believers in people’s hearts during worldly life.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r10.claim: Love for ʿAli in this interpretation means proper, non-exaggerated love.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r11.claim: The author doubts a poem about loving ʿAli, attributed to the Christian al-Rusaghni, is genuine; if the Prophetic report is authentic, it also shows the attribution is false.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r12.claim: Across the reports, the general wording governs rather than being restricted to the specific occasion of revelation.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s report: when God loves a servant He tells Gabriel to love him, announces this in heaven, and affection is placed for him on earth.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r3.claim: The merciful title fits a promise arising from mercy; the future tense suited the Meccan believers’ rejection and was fulfilled after migration as Islam strengthened.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r4.claim: One occasion report says it was revealed for the Abyssinian migrants with Jaʿfar, promising them affection in the Negus’s heart.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r5.claim: Another report says the verse came when ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, newly in Medina, grieved to leave his companions in Mecca.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r6.speaker: البراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r6.claim: Al-Baraʾ reports that the Prophet told ʿAli to ask for a covenant with God and affection in believers’ hearts, after which the verse was revealed.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r7.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says every believer loves ʿAli and his family.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r8.speaker: الإمامية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r8.claim: Imami authorities report the verse’s revelation for ʿAli from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Baqir, supporting it with a saying attributed to ʿAli about believers’ love and hypocrites’ hatred.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r9.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p143/r9.claim: A report attributed to ʿAli says that force cannot make a believer hate him or wealth make a hypocrite love him; the Prophet said believers do not hate him and hypocrites do not love him.

ELMALILI:19:77-98/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:19:77-98/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:19:77-98/r1.claim: The rendering says the Merciful will create affection for believers who do righteous deeds and make them loved in people's hearts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r1.claim: The verse contrasts believers’ affectionate fellowship at resurrection with the polytheists’ isolation in the previous verse.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r2.claim: The preceding isolation suggests condemned people wishing for a rescuer; believers instead receive affection and honor.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r3.claim: One explanation is that the Merciful gives believers angelic friends and affection among themselves, as in 41:31 and 7:43.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r4.claim: Choosing the verbal noun wudd allows it to cover several relations of affection.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r5.speaker: قتيبة بن سعيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r5.claim: A Tirmidhi report through al-Darāwardī explains that God places love for believers in the hearts of good people.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the report’s added wording a Qutaybah insertion unique to his Tirmidhi transmission.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p174/r7.claim: The most apparent explanation is that God makes love for believers from Himself, as in 20:39; commentators offered other explanations of varying merit.

TABATABAI:19:81-96/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:81-96/r1.speaker: طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة
TABATABAI:19:81-96/r1.claim: Reports from Shiite and Sunni channels say the verse was revealed concerning Ali.

TABATABAI:19:81-96/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:81-96/r2.speaker: طرق أهل السنة
TABATABAI:19:81-96/r2.claim: Some Sunni reports instead connect the revelation to the emigrants in Abyssinia; other reports give different occasions.

TABATABAI:19:81-96/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:81-96/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:81-96/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the verse wording remains general and links it to the preceding statement that the false gods will become their enemies.

TABATABAI:19:92-96/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:92-96/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:19:92-96/r11.claim: The love God promises believers is the authority and allegiance of Ali.

TABATABAI:19:96/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r1.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:19:96/r1.claim: The Prophet asks Ali to pray for a covenant and affection among believers; the verse then descends concerning Ali.

TABATABAI:19:96/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:96/r10.claim: Al-Tabataba'i glosses “miqqah” as love and says other Sunni reports based on the verse's general wording do not conflict with a specific occasion of revelation.

TABATABAI:19:96/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:19:96/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Ali and glosses its promised love as love in believers' hearts.

TABATABAI:19:96/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:19:96/r3.claim: One reported view makes the verse specific to Ali, whom every believer loves.

TABATABAI:19:96/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABATABAI:19:96/r4.claim: Al-Baqir reports that the Prophet asked Ali to pray for a covenant and love in believers' hearts, after which this verse was revealed; a similar report is attributed to Jabir.

TABATABAI:19:96/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r5.speaker: روح المعاني
TABATABAI:19:96/r5.claim: Al-Alusi infers that the verse is Medinan if this reported occasion is accepted.

TABATABAI:19:96/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:96/r6.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says none of the reports establishes that Ali's prayer occurred in Medina.

TABATABAI:19:96/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
TABATABAI:19:96/r7.claim: A report says that after migrating to Medina, Abd al-Rahman grieved leaving several companions in Mecca, and the verse was revealed.

TABATABAI:19:96/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:96/r8.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects this as a Medinan occasion because the whole sura is unanimously considered Meccan.

TABATABAI:19:96/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:96/r9.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:19:96/r9.claim: The Prophet tells Ali that the promised love is affection in the hearts of believers and the angels nearest to God, alongside other gifts bestowed on believers.

ASAD-NOTES:19:96#n80/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:96#n80/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:96#n80/r1.claim: God gives believers His love, the ability to love creation, and a place in the love of fellow people; this gift comes through revelation's guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet should patiently disregard demands to hasten punishment, depend on the Qur’an to warn and give glad tidings, and tell stubborn people the fate they will meet if they persist.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Believers receive love and welcome: angels greet them, God sends salutations, and they congratulate each other as a victorious company.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Farahi called Maryam the Rahmani surah because the name Rahman is repeated here more than in any other surah; the repetition has thematic purpose.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Christians' mistaken view made humanity eternally sinful and salvation impossible unless God's son atoned for believers' sins by sacrifice.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Jews presumed their prophetic ancestry secured them from Hell, or that any punishment would last only briefly before mercy forgave them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Arabian idolaters denied the reality of Judgment but expected God's angel-daughters to secure them through intercession if it occurred.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God's mercy does not cancel justice; both reward for truth and warning or punishment for rebellion express mercy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Forgiving rebels due to lineage, intercession, or attachment to an alleged divine son would be oppression, not mercy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Punishment can manifest mercy because wrongdoing harms creatures, while divine limits protect and develop them; criminals are not merely God's personal concern.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The surah's warnings and glad tidings are grounded in the true requirements of God's attribute al-Rahman.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r1.claim: After describing the fate of polytheists, the passage describes believers who do good; invoking al-Rahman highlights abundant mercy.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r2.claim: God creates love for believers: He loves them, makes His other servants love them, and develops brotherhood and affection among believers.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r3.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:96/r3.claim: The Prophet said that when God loves a servant He makes Gabriel, heavenly beings, and people on earth love that person; variant reports say the reverse for one God dislikes.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r1.claim: Commentators usually treat wudd, “love,” as synonymous with ḥubb, the Quran’s more usual word for love.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r10.speaker: some Sufis
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r10.claim: Some Sufis understand the ordained love as unveiling divine secrets, linking it to a hadith qudsi in which God loves the servant who draws near through supererogatory acts.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r11.speaker: al-Qushayrī
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r11.claim: Al-Qushayrī cites a related hadith qudsi in which the servant draws near until he loves God and God loves him.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r2.claim: The common interpretation is that God grants believers and righteous people love in this world, especially among other believing servants.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r3.speaker: al-Sulamī
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r3.claim: Al-Sulamī says righteous people are beloved by fellow Muslims, a manifestation of God’s love for them.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī favors the interpretation that righteous believers are loved by others.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r5.claim: An alternative interpretation is that God grants righteous believers what they themselves love; its proponents note that believers may be hated by disbelievers while some disbelievers are widely loved.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r6.speaker: the hadith
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r6.claim: A hadith supports the preferred view: when God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel to love that person, then Heaven and earth are moved to love them.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r7.claim: Some say the verse consoled ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who worried about leaving his companions in Makkah.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r8.speaker: Shiite commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r8.claim: Shiite commentators understand the ordained love as love of and spiritual attachment to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib; they hold only those who love ʿAlī to be true Muslim believers.

STUDYQURAN:19:96/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r9.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:19:96/r9.claim: A Shiite report says the Prophet told ʿAlī to ask God for a covenant and for love in believers’ hearts, after which this verse was revealed.
